p.src: Now when Xuande saw spears and swords arrayed thickly on both sides of Lady Sun's chamber, and all her maids wearing swords, he could not help turning pale. The matron stepped forward and said, “My lord, you need not be alarmed. Her ladyship has delighted in martial pursuits since childhood and ordinarily has her maids fence for her amusement. That is why you see this.” Xuande said, “Even if these are merely for her ladyship’s viewing, they chill me to the heart. Have them removed for the time being.” The matron reported to Lady Sun, “The weapons displayed in the chamber make the honored bridegroom uneasy. They should now be removed.” Lady Sun laughed and said, “After fighting for half his life, is he still afraid of weapons?” She ordered everything removed and had the maids take off their swords before attending him. That night Xuande and Lady Sun became husband and wife, and their affections were in perfect accord. Xuande also distributed gold and silk among the maids to win their goodwill, then sent Sun Qian back to Jingzhou ahead of him to report the happy news. From then on, banquets continued day after day. The Dowager treated him with the greatest affection and respect.

p.src: Meanwhile, Sun Quan sent a messenger to Chaisang Commandery to tell Zhou Yu, “My mother insisted upon it and has already married my sister to Liu Bei. I never expected our pretense to become reality. What are we to do now?” Zhou Yu was greatly startled by the news and could neither sit nor walk in peace. At length he devised a plan, wrote a secret letter, and entrusted it to the messenger to take back to Sun Quan. Sun Quan broke the seal and read the letter. In essence it said, “I never expected my scheme to end in such a reversal. Since the falsehood has become reality, we must now turn that very fact to our advantage. Liu Bei has the mettle of a hero of turbulent times; he commands such generals as Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and Zhao Yun, and moreover has Zhuge Liang to devise his strategies. He is assuredly not one who will long submit to another. In my humble opinion, nothing would be better than to keep him gently confined in Wu: build him magnificent palaces so that his ambition may be sapped; send him many beautiful women and precious curiosities to delight his eyes and ears; estrange him from Guan Yu and Zhang Fei, sever his close bond with Zhuge Liang, and station each of them in a different place. Then strike them with our troops, and the great enterprise may be settled. If he is allowed to leave now, I fear the dragon will gain the clouds and rain and prove in the end no creature of a pond. I beg my lord to consider this carefully.”

p.src: After Sun Quan had finished reading, he showed the letter to Zhang Zhao. Zhang Zhao said, “Gongjin’s plan accords exactly with my own humble opinion. Liu Bei rose from the humblest beginnings and has wandered throughout the realm. Never has he enjoyed wealth or rank. If he is now given splendid halls and lofty mansions, women, gold, and silk for his enjoyment, he will naturally grow distant from Kongming, Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, and the others. Let each of them come to resent him, and then Jingzhou may be taken. My lord should follow Gongjin’s plan and carry it out without delay.” Sun Quan was delighted. That very day he had the Eastern Residence refurbished, planted it thickly with flowers and trees, furnished it magnificently, and invited Xuande and his sister to live there; he also added several dozen female musicians, together with gold, jade, brocades, fine silks, and rare playthings. The Dowager assumed Sun Quan meant only kindness and was beside herself with joy. Xuande was indeed captivated by music and beauty and no longer gave a thought to returning to Jingzhou.

p.src: Meanwhile, Zhao Yun and his five hundred soldiers were quartered before the Eastern Residence. With nothing to do all day, they merely went outside the city to practice archery and ride their horses. As the year drew to its end, Zhao Yun suddenly recalled, “Kongming gave me three brocade pouches and instructed me to open the first as soon as I reached Nanxu; the second after remaining there until year’s end; and the third when danger left us no road of escape. Within them are marvelous and unfathomable stratagems that can ensure my lord’s return home. The year is now nearly over, and my lord, infatuated with feminine charms, will not even see me. Why not open the second pouch and act according to its plan?” He accordingly opened it and read what was inside. It proved to contain just such an ingenious scheme. That very day he went straight to the residence and requested an audience with Xuande.

p.src: A maid reported, “Zhao Zilong has come with urgent news for my lord.” Xuande summoned him in and asked what it was. Zhao Yun feigned consternation and said, “My lord, secluded here in painted halls, have you forgotten Jingzhou?” Xuande said, “What has happened to alarm you so?” Zhao Yun said, “This morning Kongming sent word that Cao Cao, bent on avenging his crushing defeat at Red Cliffs, has raised five hundred thousand picked troops and is advancing upon Jingzhou. The danger is grave, and he asks my lord to return at once.” Xuande said, “I must discuss this with my wife.” Zhao Yun said, “If you discuss it with her ladyship, she will certainly refuse to let you return. It would be better to say nothing and depart tonight. Delay will ruin the enterprise.” Xuande said, “Withdraw for the moment. I know what must be done.”

p.src: Zhao Yun deliberately pressed him several more times before withdrawing. Xuande went in to see Lady Sun and silently shed tears. Lady Sun said, “Husband, why are you troubled?” Xuande said, “I reflect that I, Bei, am adrift alone in a foreign land: while alive I cannot attend upon my parents, nor can I offer sacrifices to my ancestors. This is the gravest rebellion against filial duty. Now New Year’s Day is close at hand, and the thought fills me with unending sorrow.” Lady Sun said, “Do not try to conceal the truth from me. I have already heard everything. Zhao Zilong just reported that Jingzhou is in danger. You wish to return home and have merely used this as a pretext.” Xuande knelt and said, “Since you already know, how would I dare deceive you? If I do not go and Jingzhou is lost, I shall become the laughingstock of the realm; yet if I go, I cannot bear to leave you. That is why I am troubled.” Lady Sun said, “I have become your wife. Wherever you go, I shall follow.” Xuande said, “Though that is your wish, how could the Dowager and the Marquis of Wu ever consent to let you go? If you take pity on Liu Bei, let us part for a while.” When he had finished speaking, his tears fell like rain. Lady Sun consoled him, saying, “Husband, do not grieve. I shall earnestly plead with my mother, and she will surely allow me to go with you.” Xuande said, “Even if the Dowager consents, the Marquis of Wu will certainly prevent us.” Lady Sun pondered for a long while, then said, “When we make our New Year’s greetings, what if we say that we are going to the riverbank to sacrifice to your ancestors, and then depart without telling him?” Xuande knelt again and thanked her, saying, “If you do this, I shall never forget it, living or dead. You must not let the secret escape.”

p.src: The two settled their plan. Xuande secretly summoned Zhao Yun and instructed him, “On New Year’s Day, lead the soldiers out of the city ahead of us and wait on the main road. I shall use ancestral rites as a pretext and depart with my wife.” Zhao Yun accepted the command. On New Year’s Day, the first month of spring in the fifteenth year of Jian’an, the Marquis of Wu assembled all his civil and military officers in the great hall. Xuande and Lady Sun went in to make their obeisance to the Dowager. Lady Sun said, “My husband is thinking of the graves of his parents and ancestors, all of which lie in Zhuo Commandery, and he grieves over them day and night. Today he wishes to go to the riverbank, face north, and offer sacrifices from afar, so we have come to inform you, Mother.” The Dowager said, “That is an act of filial duty. How could I refuse? Though you never knew your husband’s parents, you may go with him to worship them. That too displays the proper duty of a wife.” Lady Sun and Xuande bowed their thanks and withdrew. At this point, Sun Quan alone was being kept in ignorance. Lady Sun entered her carriage, taking only the valuables needed for the journey. Xuande mounted his horse and rode out of the city with several horsemen, then joined Zhao Yun. With five hundred soldiers guarding them before and behind, they left Nanxu and pressed forward with all speed.

p.src: That day Sun Quan became thoroughly drunk, and his attendants supported him into the rear hall; the civil and military officers all dispersed. By the time the officials discovered that Xuande and his wife had fled, night had already fallen. They wished to report it to Sun Quan, but he was too drunk to wake. When at last he awoke, it was already the fifth watch. The next day, when Sun Quan learned that Xuande had escaped, he hurriedly summoned his civil and military officers to deliberate. Zhang Zhao said, “Now that this man has escaped, sooner or later he is certain to cause trouble. You must pursue him at once.” Sun Quan ordered Chen Wu and Pan Zhang to select five hundred elite troops and, without pausing by day or night, overtake Xuande and seize him. The two commanders accepted the order and departed. Sun Quan bitterly resented Xuande and dashed the jade inkstone upon his desk to fragments. Cheng Pu said, “My lord, your rage may reach the heavens, but in my judgment Chen Wu and Pan Zhang will never capture that man.” Sun Quan said, “How dare they disobey my command?” Cheng Pu said, “Since childhood, the Lady has delighted in martial affairs; she is stern, resolute, and upright, and all the commanders fear her. Since she has consented to follow Liu Bei, she will surely depart of one heart with him. When the pursuing commanders see the Lady, how could they bring themselves to strike?” Sun Quan flew into a rage, drew the sword at his side, and summoned Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai to receive his command: “Take this sword and bring me the heads of my sister and Liu Bei! Whoever disobeys shall be beheaded at once!” Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai accepted the command, then led three thousand troops in pursuit.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande whipped on his horse, gave it the rein, and hurried along. That night he rested by the roadside for only two watches before rising in haste and setting out again. As they neared the border of Chaisang, they saw a great cloud of dust rising behind them, and someone reported, “The pursuers are here!” Alarmed, Xuande asked Zhao Yun, “The pursuing troops are upon us. What are we to do?” Zhao Yun replied, “My lord, go on ahead. I shall guard the rear.” As they rounded the foot of the mountain ahead, a body of troops barred their way. At their head were two great commanders, who shouted sternly, “Liu Bei, dismount at once and submit to bondage! By Commander-in-Chief Zhou’s order, we have long awaited you here!” It turned out that Zhou Yu, fearing Xuande might escape, had earlier sent Xu Sheng and Ding Feng with three thousand troops to encamp and wait at this strategic point. He continually ordered men to climb the heights and watch from afar, calculating that if Xuande took the overland route, he must pass this way. That day, Xu Sheng and Ding Feng saw Xuande’s party approaching; each snatched up his weapon and blocked the road. Xuande was panic-stricken. Reining his horse around, he asked Zhao Yun, “Troops bar us in front, and pursuers press us from behind. With no road forward or back, what are we to do?” Zhao Yun said, “Do not be alarmed, my lord. The strategist devised three wondrous schemes, each kept in a brocade pouch. Two have already been opened, and both proved true. The third remains here; he instructed me to open it only when we encountered grave danger. Today our peril is urgent; we should open it and see.” He thereupon opened the brocade pouch and presented its contents to Xuande.

p.src: After reading it, Xuande hurried to the front of the column and tearfully appealed to Lady Sun: “I have words from the depths of my heart, and now I must tell you the whole truth.” She said, “Husband, whatever you have to say, tell me truthfully.” Xuande said, “Formerly the Marquis of Wu and Zhou Yu plotted together to take Liu Bei as the Lady’s husband. In truth, it was not done for your sake, but only to imprison Liu Bei and seize Jingzhou. Once Jingzhou was taken, they would certainly kill me. Thus they used you as fragrant bait with which to hook me. I came though ten thousand deaths held no terror for me, because I knew you possessed the spirit of a true hero and would surely take pity on me. Yesterday I heard that the Marquis of Wu intended to harm me, so I pretended that Jingzhou was in peril in order to devise our return. Fortunately, you did not forsake me and have come with me this far. Now the Marquis of Wu has sent men in pursuit behind us, while Zhou Yu has sent others to bar our way ahead. None but you can deliver us from this calamity. If you will not consent, I beg to die before your carriage and thus repay your kindness.”

p.src: The Lady said angrily, “Since my brother does not regard me as his own flesh and blood, how could I have the face to meet him again? I shall resolve today’s danger myself.” She ordered her attendants to push the carriage straight forward, raised its curtain, and personally shouted at Xu Sheng and Ding Feng, “Are you two trying to rebel?” Xu Sheng and Ding Feng hurriedly dismounted, cast aside their weapons, and stood before the carriage to answer: “How would we dare rebel? We received Commander-in-Chief Zhou’s military order to station troops here and wait expressly for Liu Bei.” Lady Sun cried furiously, “Zhou Yu, that traitorous villain! We of the Southland have never treated you unjustly! Xuande is an Imperial Uncle of the great Han and is my husband. I already informed my mother and brother that we were returning to Jingzhou. Why, then, have you two brought troops to this mountainside to block the road? Do you mean to rob my husband and me of our belongings?” Xu Sheng and Ding Feng repeatedly murmured assent and said, “We would not dare. Please calm your anger, my Lady. This has nothing to do with us; it is Commander-in-Chief Zhou’s military order.” Lady Sun rebuked them: “You fear only Zhou Yu; do you not fear me? If Zhou Yu can kill you, can I not kill Zhou Yu?” After roundly abusing Zhou Yu, she ordered the carriage pushed onward. Xu Sheng and Ding Feng thought, “We are but subordinates. How would we dare defy the Lady?” Seeing also that Zhao Yun was bristling with fury, they had no choice but to call their troops aside and open a broad road for the party to pass.

p.src: They had gone scarcely five or six li when Chen Wu and Pan Zhang overtook them from behind. Xu Sheng and Ding Feng related the whole affair. Chen Wu and Pan Zhang said, “You were wrong to let him pass. We have come expressly by the Marquis of Wu’s command to pursue and seize him and take him back.” The four commanders then joined their forces and hurried onward in pursuit. As Xuande traveled on, he suddenly heard a great clamor rising behind him. Once again Xuande appealed to Lady Sun: “The pursuing troops have come again. What are we to do?” She said, “Husband, go on ahead. Zilong and I will guard the rear.” Xuande led three hundred troops ahead toward the riverbank. Zilong reined in beside the carriage and arrayed the soldiers to await the approaching commanders. When the four commanders saw Lady Sun, they could only dismount and stand with hands clasped in salute. The Lady said, “Chen Wu, Pan Zhang, what brings you here?” The two commanders replied, “By our lord’s command, we have come to ask the Lady and Xuande to return.” With a stern expression, the Lady rebuked them: “It is worthless fellows like you who sow discord between my brother and me! I am already married, and in returning today I am certainly not eloping with a stranger. I act upon my mother’s gracious command that my husband and I return to Jingzhou. Even if my brother himself came, he would still have to observe proper courtesy. Do you two mean to rely on the might of your troops and murder me?” Her abuse left the four men exchanging glances, each thinking, “For ten thousand years they will still be brother and sister. Moreover, the Dowager herself sanctioned this; and the Marquis of Wu is a most filial son—how would he dare oppose his mother’s word? If tomorrow he changes his mind, the fault will lie solely with us. We would do better to grant them this favor.” Nor could they see Xuande among the troops; they saw only Zhao Yun glaring fiercely, ready for battle. The four commanders therefore repeatedly murmured assent and withdrew. Lady Sun ordered the carriage pushed onward at once. Xu Sheng said, “Let the four of us go together to see Commander-in-Chief Zhou and report this matter.”

u.src: They had gone scarcely five or six li when Chen Wu and Pan Zhang overtook them from behind.
Xu Sheng and Ding Feng related the whole affair.
Chen Wu and Pan Zhang said, “You were wrong to let him pass.
We have come expressly by the Marquis of Wu’s command to pursue and seize him and take him back.”
The four commanders then joined their forces and hurried onward in pursuit.
As Xuande traveled on, he suddenly heard a great clamor rising behind him.
Once again Xuande appealed to Lady Sun: “The pursuing troops have come again. What are we to do?”
She said, “Husband, go on ahead. Zilong and I will guard the rear.”
Xuande led three hundred troops ahead toward the riverbank.
Zilong reined in beside the carriage and arrayed the soldiers to await the approaching commanders.
When the four commanders saw Lady Sun, they could only dismount and stand with hands clasped in salute.
The Lady said, “Chen Wu, Pan Zhang, what brings you here?”
The two commanders replied, “By our lord’s command, we have come to ask the Lady and Xuande to return.”
With a stern expression, the Lady rebuked them: “It is worthless fellows like you who sow discord between my brother and me!
I am already married, and in returning today I am certainly not eloping with a stranger.
I act upon my mother’s gracious command that my husband and I return to Jingzhou.
Even if my brother himself came, he would still have to observe proper courtesy.
Do you two mean to rely on the might of your troops and murder me?”
Her abuse left the four men exchanging glances, each thinking, “For ten thousand years they will still be brother and sister.
Moreover, the Dowager herself sanctioned this;
and the Marquis of Wu is a most filial son—how would he dare oppose his mother’s word?
If tomorrow he changes his mind, the fault will lie solely with us.
We would do better to grant them this favor.”
Nor could they see Xuande among the troops;
they saw only Zhao Yun glaring fiercely, ready for battle.
The four commanders therefore repeatedly murmured assent and withdrew.
Lady Sun ordered the carriage pushed onward at once.
Xu Sheng said, “Let the four of us go together to see Commander-in-Chief Zhou and report this matter.”

p.src: While the four generals still hesitated, an army suddenly swept toward them like a whirlwind; looking closer, they saw Jiang Qin and Zhou Tai. The two generals asked, “Have you seen Liu Bei?” The four replied, “He passed by early this morning. Half a day has gone by since then.” Jiang Qin said, “Why did you not seize him?” The four related what Lady Sun had said to them. Jiang Qin said, “The Marquis of Wu feared precisely this. He entrusted me with a sealed sword and ordered that we first kill his sister and then behead Liu Bei. Anyone who disobeys is to be executed at once!” The four generals said, “They have already gone far. What can we do?” Jiang Qin said, “In the end, most of his men are infantry and cannot march swiftly. Generals Xu and Ding, ride swiftly to report to the Commander and have him send fast boats in pursuit by water; the other four of us will pursue them along the bank. Whether by water or by land, once we catch them, kill them without listening to a word they say.” Thereupon Xu Sheng and Ding Feng rode swiftly to report to Zhou Yu; while Jiang Qin, Zhou Tai, Chen Wu, and Pan Zhang led their troops in pursuit along the river.

p.src: Meanwhile, Xuande and his company had traveled a considerable distance from Chaisang. When they reached Liulangpu, his heart eased a little. They followed the riverbank in search of a crossing, but as far as they could see, the broad waters stretched before them without a single boat. Xuande bowed his head in troubled thought. Zhao Yun said, “My lord has escaped from the tiger’s jaws and is now near our own borders. I am certain the Military Adviser has made arrangements. Why be anxious or doubtful?” Hearing this, Xuande suddenly remembered the splendors he had enjoyed in Eastern Wu, and tears of sorrow fell unbidden. A later poet lamented this in verse:

p.src: Xuande ordered Zhao Yun to scout ahead for boats, but suddenly a report came that dust was billowing skyward behind them. Xuande climbed to high ground and looked. Seeing troops and horses advancing across the land, he sighed, “We have fled for days, and both men and horses are exhausted. Now the pursuers are upon us again—there is nowhere left to die!” The shouts drew steadily nearer. At the height of their panic, they suddenly saw more than twenty covered boats moored in a row along the riverbank. Zhao Yun said, “By Heaven’s grace, there are boats here! Let us row to the opposite bank and decide what to do next!”

p.src: Xuande and Lady Sun immediately hurried aboard. Zilong led the five hundred soldiers aboard as well. Then a man in a silk headdress and Daoist robe emerged from the cabin, laughing heartily, and said, “Rejoice, my lord! Zhuge Liang has been waiting here for a long time.” Those aboard who were disguised as travelers were all sailors from Jingzhou. Xuande was overjoyed. Before long, the four generals arrived in pursuit. Kongming pointed laughingly at the men on the bank and said, “I foresaw all this long ago. Go back and tell Zhou Yu that he should never again resort to schemes involving beautiful women.” A disorderly volley of arrows flew from the bank, but the boats had already drawn far away. Jiang Qin and the other three generals could only stare after them in helpless dismay.

p.src: As Xuande and Kongming proceeded, the river suddenly resounded with a tremendous roar. Looking back, they saw countless warships. Beneath the banner bearing the character “Commander,” Zhou Yu personally led his seasoned marines, with Huang Gai on his left and Han Dang on his right. They came as swiftly as galloping horses and as fast as shooting stars. When they were nearly overtaken, Kongming ordered the boats rowed to the northern bank. They abandoned the vessels, all went ashore, and continued their journey with the carts and horses. When Zhou Yu reached the riverbank, his men likewise disembarked and pursued them. All the naval troops, officers and men alike, went on foot. Only the leading officers rode horses. Zhou Yu rode foremost, closely followed by Huang Gai, Han Dang, Xu Sheng, and Ding Feng. Zhou Yu asked, “What place is this?” A soldier replied, “Ahead lies the border of Huangzhou.” Seeing Xuande’s troops not far ahead, Zhou Yu ordered his men to exert all their strength in pursuit.

p.src: In the midst of the pursuit, a drum suddenly sounded, and a band of swordsmen surged out from a mountain valley. The great general at their head was none other than Guan Yunchang. Zhou Yu lost his composure and hastily wheeled his horse to flee. Yunchang pursued him, and Zhou Yu spurred his horse onward for his life. As he fled, Huang Zhong charged out from the left and Wei Yan from the right, each at the head of an army. The troops of Wu suffered a crushing defeat. Just as Zhou Yu hastily boarded his ship, the soldiers on the bank shouted in unison, “Zhou Yu’s wondrous scheme was to bring peace to the realm—but he lost both the lady and his troops!” Zhou Yu cried furiously, “Let us go ashore again and fight them to the death!” Huang Gai and Han Dang held him back with all their strength. Zhou Yu thought to himself, “My scheme has failed. How can I show my face before the Marquis of Wu?” With a great cry, his wounded flesh burst open, and he collapsed upon the deck. The generals hastened to aid him, but he had already lost consciousness. Truly:
